newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France pilots to seek shares pact.
newsitem.headline: Air France pilots to seek shares pact.

text.p: The Air France SNPL pilots union council is due to meet on Friday but is not expected to call for a continuation of its four-day strike, a union spokesman said on Thursday.
Union officials are expected to present proposals to management for an agreement on employees' shareholdings in the airline, the spokesman said.

The signature by the SPAC pilots union on Tuesday of a two-tier pay scale allows Air France to apply the new salary scheme to all pilots, even though five other unions did not sign, an Air France spokeswoman said.
Air France chairman Christian Blanc has said he wants employees to hold between 20 to 30 percent of the capital as part of the group's privatisation.
The SNPL has been in the forefront of the current strike called to oppose the introduction of the new pay system which allows Air France to hire 450 new pilots at lower salaries than existing crews.
Of the Air France group's 3,100 pilots, 1,650 are members of the SNPL, the union official said. Four other unions opposed the new pay plan.
"We are not opposed to an overall effort but we are opposed to the 450 young people being targeted since they have had to go into debt to pay for their training," the SNPL spokesman said.

The new pay scheme means pilots with more than 3,000 hours flying time will receive gross annual pay of 320,000 francs in the first two years of service, while less experienced pilots will get 240,000 in the first year.

The 450 pilots who will be hired over the next three years will be paid at the higher level, which compares to annual salary of 350,000 francs paid to the last batch of pilots taken on before a hiring freeze in 1993.
